findings.reason: the worker must open a resolved followup to recover prior art and may rebuild a landed repair or miss an open one.
findings.text: §5 cites prior art by outcome ("the already-landed session attachment or first promotion repair") but never names reckon/crew/promotion.py nor which of the six S16 promotion-truth repairs are still open, so its own guard "without rebuilding what landed" cannot be checked from the brief

findings.reason: naming one interface (a single outcome-truth adjudication) before dispatch keeps the module's surface smaller than what it hides instead of accreting more of the same machinery.
findings.text: the residual committed/merged/content-surviving distinctions are given no single adjudication entry point, so they land in reckon/crew/promotion.py (9,009 lines, already the largest crew module) as separate predicates over the same run record

findings.reason: a parallel validator forks the readiness logic roadmap.py owns and the two will drift, so §2 should name roadmap.py as the owner to extend rather than add a second implementation.
findings.text: §2 (docs/plans/execution-orchestration-hardening.html:35) proposes first-class sprint proposal/validate/close checking one-active-sprint, dependency readiness, duplicate membership, capacity and evidence gates, but readiness and gates are already owned by roadmap.execution_gates, roadmap.closure_blockers and roadmap._dispatchability, with evidence gates in reckon/evidence.py
